errors.english: is not wearing the community's cloth
errors.why: In this robe-distribution context (rain without a roof, dyeing, bowl-work as occasions) bgo means to apportion/distribute: the Sangha's cloth is not to be distributed; the same applies to the following 'mi bgo na', rendered 'If it is not worn'.

errors.english: if one person comes to receive the cloth entrusted to four people
errors.why: བཞིས is instrumental: the cloth was deposited by four people, and one of them comes to take it back, not cloth entrusted to four.

note: A careful rendering of a terse Vinaya commentary; the main doubt is reading bgo as 'wear' where the topic is distributing robe-cloth.

errors.english: Remoteness in the case of inference is merely the opposite of subtlety of nature.
errors.why: མ་བསྐལ་བ is non-remoteness: for inference, non-remoteness is merely the absence of subtlety of nature.

fix.find: Remoteness in the case of inference
fix.replace: Non-remoteness in the case of inference

note: Accurate on the observable/unobservable and substance/quality argument apart from one dropped negation.

errors.english: are in every way of a nonexistent nature, because they are not apprehended in any way
errors.why: ཇི་ལྟར་ཡང་ (kathaṃcit) means 'in some respect', as the translator renders it in the parallel verses; the Jaina example claims self, pot etc. are in some respect non-existent because in some respect not apprehended, not absolutely.

fix.find: are in every way of a nonexistent nature, because they are not apprehended in any way
fix.replace: are in some respect of a nonexistent nature, because in some respect they are not apprehended

errors.why: The unmarked inserted gloss is misleading: the term means the impossibility (non-occurrence) of the reason otherwise, i.e. without the probandum, not 'inconceivability'.

note: The kārikās are rendered as prose with unmarked glosses inserted, but the argument is followed correctly except for the kathaṃcit verse.

errors.english: Even if the vocal object [note: sound] does not by its very nature possess a variegated conjunction
errors.why: སྒྲའི་ཡུལ is the referent of the word: the objection is that even if conjunction is not strictly the referent of the word 'variegated', it is called so metaphorically; nothing about sound is meant.

fix.find: Even if the vocal object [note: sound] does not by its very nature possess a variegated conjunction
fix.replace: Even if conjunction is not, in the strict sense, the referent of the word "variegated"

errors.english: various conjunctions of blue and other colors exist
errors.why: The opponent posits a variegated conjunction (citra saṃyoga) of blue etc., which is exactly what the reply denies ('conjunction is not variegated'); 'various conjunctions' loses the point.

errors.english: a mere metaphor cannot be the basis. This applies directly to the concept of conjunction.
errors.why: The root says '[conjunction] is not the basis of mere metaphor', and the commentary tells us to supply 'conjunction' as subject; the English makes the metaphor the subject.

note: The Vaiśeṣika conjunction argument is mostly followed, but the key objection about the word's referent is misread as being about sound.
Faithful rendering of the commentary's verse glosses and compound analyses.

errors.english: to counteract the abandonment of non-virtuous phenomena
errors.why: Right view etc. are cultivated as the antidote that abandons the non-virtuous dharmas such as wrong view, not to counteract their abandonment.

fix.find: to counteract the abandonment of non-virtuous phenomena
fix.replace: as the antidote that abandons non-virtuous phenomena

errors.english: It is that which is not motivated by views of a noble being, a worldly being, a self
errors.why: 'Noble, supramundane' (āryā lokottarā) qualifies right view itself; the list of views it is not motivated by begins with self, sentient being, etc.

fix.find: It is that which is not motivated by views of a noble being, a worldly being, a self
fix.replace: It is the noble, supramundane view that is not motivated by views of a self

errors.why: In a list with virtue and non-virtue, ལུང་དུ་བསྟན་པ is the morally determinate (vyākṛta, vs. avyākṛta 'neutral'), not prophecy.

note: Readable, but the Akṣayamati quotation is mis-segmented and the antidote sentence is inverted.

errors.english: From mental projections, the fire of the limbs arises
errors.why: ཡན་ལག་མེད is Anaṅga, the Bodiless (Kāma): from imagining arises the fire of Love (anaṅgāgni), not a 'fire of the limbs'.

errors.english: the body of those with blind minds is thinned day by day by limbs that fail to see faults
errors.why: The 'missing limb/organ for seeing faults' describes the blind-minded lover (or is Anaṅga as agent), not limbs that thin the body.

errors.english: They embrace women who are like a blazing fire born of iron and pervaded by sparks.
errors.why: This is the hell punishment itself: the adulterer embraces a woman made of blazing iron covered in sparks; 'like' turns it into a simile.

note: The ornate verses are rendered as prose and several kāvya images (Anaṅga, the iron woman of hell) are misread, though the overall drift is right.
A faithful rendering of the word-by-word commentary on the tigress episode.

errors.why: འཁྲུལ་པ here is deviation (vyabhicāra), i.e. the inconclusive reason (anaikāntika), not 'inconsistency'.
The phrase is 'proving the probandum' (sādhyasādhana), taken as the converse of 'proving through dissimilarity', not establishing through the probandum.

note: Follows a difficult Pramāṇa argument on qualifying the reason reasonably well; a few technical phrasings are loose.

errors.english: because what does not remain to destroy it itself remains
errors.why: If perishing depends on another, a cause of remaining is pointless because, as long as the destroyer is absent, the thing remains of itself.

fix.find: because what does not remain to destroy it itself remains
fix.replace: because, so long as what destroys it is absent, it remains of itself

note: Sound rendering of the refutation of the body as support of the mind, with one garbled reason clause.
